Subject: Re: POC traffic — quick debugging notes

Marcus/team — quick notes from initial pass: bullets
- We replayed the provided Nimbus logs against Gateway traces. Several failing requests show our auth validation returning an internal error path when the upstream JWT library timed out calling the JWKS endpoint. Instead of mapping to a 401/498, the error bubbles up and becomes a 502/503 in the gateway.
- We also observed short-lived clock skew on a subset of Nimbus's token issuer nodes (~120s drift) during bursts; tokens with small leeway were intermittently rejected in validation reconnaissance, but errors were inconsistent.
- Client-side retry behaviour (Nimbus SDK) is aggressive: immediate retry x3 on these failures. Retries are exacerbating the congestion and creating more jwks lookups, which increases the JWKS latency.

Immediate mitigations I recommend now: bullets
1) Gatekeeper: change classifier so token validation timeouts map to 4xx (explicit 498 or 401) so client retries back off quickly. This avoids considering them as upstream server failure.
2) Cache: increase JWKS cache TTL on gateway for the POC tenant to reduce external JWKS storms (short-term config).
3) Client guidance: ask Nimbus to enable exponential backoff and jitter in their SDK, and to temporarily reduce parallelism in the 30s ingest window.

We'll prepare a minimal patch to the classifier; Olga, can you stage a config flip and the patch? I'll open a Jira.

Rishi
Director, Serving Runtime

Subject: Re: POC traffic — temporary mitigation deployed

Doing the quick mitigation now — summary of actions performed: bullets
- Flipped gateway classifier to map token validation timeouts / JWKS fetch timeouts -> 498 (token validation error) for tenant-scoped traffic (Nimbus POC). This will stop classification as 502/503.
- Increased JWKS cache TTL from 60s -> 600s for Nimbus's tenant to reduce external jitter.
- Deployed a lightweight rate-limiter on the JWKS fetch path and added circuit-breaker to avoid cascading slowdowns when issuer is slow.
- Disabled one of the redundant validation threads that was generating duplicate external JWKS pulls in some code paths.

Patch and short patch notes attached: [Attachment: gateway_classify_patch.diff]

Expected outcome: should collapse output 5xx volume and surface 498/401 quickly so clients can back off. We will watch for latency impact of the cache increase.

Olga

Katie — thanks for the quick confirmation. Brief executive summary and next steps below (for Nimbus CTO & procurement): bullets
- What happened: During Nimbus' POC ingest bursts our Gateway misclassified token validation timeouts (JWKS fetch timeouts and transient clock-skew rejects) as upstream server errors. Those 5xx/429 designations triggered client retries that amplified JWKS traffic and caused a self-reinforcing surge.
- What we did now: Adjusted classifier to return 498 for token validation issues, increased JWKS cache TTL, added circuit-breaker to JWKS path, and disabled duplicate validation threads. Nimbus reduced their SDK retry aggressiveness. Immediate impact: 5xx volume down ~85%, retries reduced roughly 70% in recent windows.
- Root-cause action items (owned): bullets
  - INF-9248 (Rishi/Olga): formal patch to gatekeeper classifier + unit/regression tests to ensure token timeouts are mapped to 4xx. ETA: 48 hours.
  - INF-9251 (Infra): long-term JWKS cache strategy and TTL negotiation with issuer owners. ETA: 2 weeks.
  - CS/Billing (Laura/Sean): credit evaluation for Nimbus POC window; Sean, please take lead.
  - Customer SDK (Nimbus): implement exponential backoff + jitter; Redwood will provide recommended config.

I'll create the Jira tickets and draft the formal customer note. Sean/Laura — please coordinate credit request and the customer-facing post-mortem. Rishi/Olga — ping me if you need a 2pm sync.
